# Places API Permitted Uses for Customers with a Billing Address in the European Economic Area (EEA)

In this Places API Permitted Uses document, “Places API” means both the Places API Legacy and Places API New services.

Subject to the [EEA Places API Service Specific Terms](/terms/maps-platform/eea/maps-service-terms), Customers with a billing address in the EEA may only use the Google Maps Content from the Places API within Customer Applications to (collectively, the “Permitted Uses”):

(1) facilitate address lookup and autocompletion functionalities;

(2) display information about Customer’s physical stores, offices, or official service points;

(3) enable Customers to visualize and manage Places content related to a sales team’s customers or opportunities;

(4) enable users to associate tasks, notes, or reminders with specific named places within a productivity, chat, personal organization, or note-taking functionality;

(5) show information about nearby points of interest (e.g., schools, parks, grocery stores) to provide context for a real estate listing or rental property being viewed by the user;

(6) show information about a Place related to a financial transaction;

(7) integrate Places as points of interest or objectives within a game;

(8) allow users to tag or share a specific Place in their posts, event creations, or shared experiences within a social platform; and

(9) allow users to set and monitor location context for their personal smart home routines or IoT device actions.

Effective **8 July 2025** , new **EEA-specific Google Maps Platform Terms of Service (EEA terms)** will impact how you build applications and experiences for users if your project is linked to an EEA billing account.

We strongly recommend that you read and understand the [announcement](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/faq), as the details potentially impact your existing and new applications that integrate Google Maps Platform.

This document describes **usage and Google Maps Platform functionality changes** for the **Places API** and related services.

The information described in this document reflects the [EEA terms governing your use of Google Maps Platform Services](https://cloud.google.com/terms/maps-platform/eea) as of 8 July 2025, which may change over time. For the most recent and binding terms applicable to you, please see your Google Maps Platform Agreement with Google.

## Affected services All Places API (New and Legacy) methods are affected. The affected services in the Places API (New and Legacy) include the following capabilities: Place Details, Text Search, Nearby Search, Autocomplete, Place Autocomplete, Query Autocomplete, Find Place, Current Place, and Place Photos.

The Places API (New and Legacy) also includes Places API service availability through the Places Javascript API (New and Legacy), the Places SDK for Android (New and Legacy), and the Places SDK for iOS (New and Legacy).

These changes do not apply to the Places UI Kit.
## Places API adjustments for EEA customers These adjustments apply to (a) projects created after 8 July 2025 that are linked to an account with an EEA billing address, and/or to (b) projects that are no longer in the [Unmodified State](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/faq#material-modification) after 8 July 2025. The following table summarizes the adjustments, delineated in the [EEA Service Specific Terms](https://cloud.google.com/terms/maps-platform/eea/maps-service-terms), for each Google Maps Platform service. | Places API Functionality Adjustments | Terms of Service Changes | |---|---| | None | *No Use With any Map*. Other than latitude, longitude, and place_id, Customer must not use Google Maps Content from the Places API With any Map. *Permitted Use*. Other than latitude, longitude, and place_id, Customer may only use the Google Maps Content from the Places API as permitted by the [Places API EEA Permitted Uses](https://cloud.google.com/terms/maps-platform/eea-places-api-permitted-uses). \*\*\*For clarity, the restrictions above---No Use With any Map and Permitted Use---do not apply to the Places UI Kit.\*\*\* | ## Examples of "With any Map" and "without a map" The EEA terms changes affect how you use Google Maps Content from this service "With any Map." "With any Map" means to display Google Maps Content on, next to, or in a manner that is visually associated with any map, including a Google map, or to link Google Maps Content to any map or link any map to Google Maps Content (unless the specific map being linked to is the source of the applicable Google Maps Content). For clarity, you may continue to link to the Google Maps Content source links provided by the Service (for example, [`googleMapsLinks`](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/places/web-service/place-details#required-parameters) in the Places API). The following examples are illustrations of what "With any Map" and "without a map" can look like, to help you comply with the terms of your Agreement. The examples are not comprehensive. Ultimately, you are responsible for complying with the terms of your Agreement. |---|---| | ![Blue dot that is used in subsequent examples](https://developers.google.com/static/maps/comms/eea/images/with-map-dot.png) | The blue circles in the following examples represent Google Maps Content from Google Maps Platform Services. | |---|---|---| | ![A map with a blue dot](https://developers.google.com/static/maps/comms/eea/images/with-map-on-map.png) | ![A map with blue dots next to it](https://developers.google.com/static/maps/comms/eea/images/with-map-next-to-map.png) | ![A map with a list blue dots separated by text, with a map with blue dots on the other side of the text.](https://developers.google.com/static/maps/comms/eea/images/with-map-visually-associated.png) | |---|---|---| | ![A map with a blue dot that links to a map in a new window.](https://developers.google.com/static/maps/comms/eea/images/with-map-link-to-uikit.png) | ![A list of blue dots with no map being displayed.](https://developers.google.com/static/maps/comms/eea/images/without-map.png) | |
## Alternative integrations

The following integration guidelines and examples are provided to help you visually implement the Places API as it relates to the requirement for no use of Google Maps Content With any Map. As a reminder, your use of Google Maps Content from the Places API must also comply with the [Places API EEA Permitted Uses](https://cloud.google.com/terms/maps-platform/eea-places-api-permitted-uses).

- You may still use latitude, longitude, and Place ID from the Places API With any Map. This includes linking using only the latitude, longitude, or Place ID to a map as long as other Google Maps Content is not used With any Map. |---|---|---| | ![](https://developers.google.com/static/maps/comms/eea/images/with-map-link-to-map.png) | ![](https://developers.google.com/static/maps/comms/eea/images/with-map-lat-long.png) | | | *An example of linking to a map using latitude, longitude, or Place ID, which is still permitted* | *An example of latitude and longitude on a map, which is still permitted* | |
- You may continue to use the Places API Service in permitted situations where the Google Maps Content is not used With any Map. |---|---| | ![](https://developers.google.com/static/maps/comms/eea/images/without-map.png) | | | *An example of using Places API Content without a map.* | |
- You may use the Places API in combination with Places UI Kit where appropriate for your application. |---|---| | ![](https://developers.google.com/static/maps/comms/eea/images/with-map-link-to-uikit.png) | | | *An example of linking to a map using Place ID where Places UI Kit is shown next to the Map* | |
- In most other situations, Places UI Kit is available for use With any Map.
### Places UI Kit Google Maps Platform includes Places UI Kit, which lets you build integrations to help your users visualize Places content with any map, or without any map. The [Places API Permitted Uses](https://cloud.google.com/terms/maps-platform/eea-places-api-permitted-uses) restrictions don't apply to the Places UI Kit. For example, Places UI Kit lets you display Place Details on a map or render a List of Places from a search next to a map, as illustrated in the following image. ![A list of places next to a map. One marker is selected, and its details are shown on the map.](https://developers.google.com/static/maps/comms/eea/images/uikit-with-places.png) > [!NOTE] > **Note:** Places UI Kit elements for Place Details, Place Autocomplete, and Place Search will be generally available in mid-July 2025. Use the following resources to help you build with Places UI Kit: **Integration guides** - [Adopt Places UI Kit for Existing Places API Users](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/javascript/adopt-places-ui-kit) - [Discover Places with Place Search Element and Maps JavaScript API](https://developers.google.com/maps/architecture/discover-with-place-search-element) - [Build an Interactive Store Finder with Places UI Kit](https://developers.google.com/maps/architecture/ui-kit-store-finder) **Places UI Kit product documentation** - [JavaScript](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/javascript/places-ui-kit/overview) - [Android](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/places/android-sdk/places-ui-kit-overview) - [iOS](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/places/ios-sdk/places-ui-kit-overview) ### Road safety EEA customers may now use Google Maps Platform Services, where suitable, in embedded vehicle systems. They may also use Google Maps Platform Services, where suitable, for real-time navigation with a third-party map, as long as that real-time navigation usage complies with Google's safety requirements. Due to road safety risks that can arise under these new terms, Google now requires that developers adhere to [safety requirements](https://cloud.google.com/terms/maps-platform/eea-safety-requirements) in order to, for example, limit the risks of mismatched roads. > [!NOTE] > **Note:** Use of Google Maps Platform Services in embedded vehicle systems in the EEA occurs at each Customer's own discretion, and the Customer is responsible for compliance with any applicable laws, regulations, industry standards, or other requirements. ## What if I have additional questions not covered in this document? If you have any technical questions not addressed in this document or the [General FAQ](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/faq), you can contact [Google Maps Platform Support](https://developers.google.com/maps/support?utm_medium=MSA&utm_source=GMP_Billing_Admin&utm_campaign=Dec_24&utm_content=GMP_Support). If you have a negotiated agreement with Google and have questions about your contract, you can contact your Google Maps Platform representative. If you are unsure who your account representative is, reach out using our [Contact Sales form](https://mapsplatform.google.com/contact-us/?utm_medium=MSA&utm_source=GMP_Billing_Admin&utm_campaign=Dec_24&utm_content=Contact_Sales).

The Google Maps Content from the Places API (New and Legacy) may no longer be displayed with any map, including a Google Map. - Certain content from some Google Maps Platform Services will no longer be returned due to our standards for Google Maps Content. - EEA customers may now, where suitable, use Google Maps Platform Services in embedded vehicle systems. They may also use Google Maps Platform Services, where suitable, for real-time navigation with a third-party map, as long as that real-time navigation usage complies with Google's safety requirements. More comprehensive details on these services and terms changes are available in this document and related service-specific integration guides. This document addresses common questions regarding the following: - [Affected customers](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/faq#affected-customers) - [EEA-specific Google Maps Platform Terms of Service](https://cloud.google.com/terms/maps-platform/eea) - [EEA-specific Google Maps Platform Services and Service Specific Terms](https://cloud.google.com/terms/maps-platform/eea/maps-service-terms) - [Your current integration of Google Maps Platform prior to 8 July 2025](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/faq#current-integration) - [Other questions](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/faq#other-questions) If this document has been updated, it will be reflected in the change log at the bottom of this page. ## Affected Customers ### Who is affected by these changes? All projects linked to billing accounts with an address in the EEA ("EEA customers") are affected by these changes starting **8 July 2025**. | Before 8 July 2025 | On or after 8 July 2025 | |---|---| | If your project was created before **8 July 2025** : You can continue your current use of Google Maps Platform Services, as long as you do not [materially modify your integration](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/faq#material-modification) on or after **8 July 2025**. | If your project is created on or after **8 July 2025** , or if you [materially modify your existing integration](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/faq#material-modification) on or after **8 July 2025** , your project will be subject to the EEA-specific [Google Maps Platform ToS](https://cloud.google.com/terms/maps-platform/eea), which incorporates the EEA-Specific [Google Maps Platform Service Specific Terms](https://cloud.google.com/terms/maps-platform/eea/maps-service-terms) and [services modifications](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/faq#sst-updates). | ## EEA-specific Google Maps Platform Terms of Service ### What updates are we making to our Terms of Service? We are introducing an [**EEA ToS**](https://cloud.google.com/terms/maps-platform/eea). This version removes three provisions from the "Restrictions Against Misusing the Services" section of your Agreement: 1. No Re-Creating Google Products or Features 2. No Use with Non-Google Maps 3. No Use in Embedded Vehicle Systems We will remove clauses with the same meaning or effect as the above listed clauses in all other applicable contractual terms that govern your use of Google Maps Platform, including the Google Maps Platform Service Specific Terms. The EEA ToS will also include: - (1) Improved organization through clause rearrangement. - (2) Clarified restrictions on using Google Maps Content for AI/ML by adding a new example. - (3) Added requirements for customers to ensure: (a) authorized third parties uphold the Agreement and (b) responsibility for data misalignment and distinguishing Google content from non-Google content. If you have a negotiated agreement with Google, refer to the question, [How do these updates impact me if I have a negotiated agreement with Google?](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/faq#negotiated-agreement) ## EEA-specific Google Maps Platform Services and Service Specific Terms ### Will there be any updates to Services and Service Specific Terms? We are modifying some Google Maps Platform Services and Service Specific Terms. These include modified responses for some APIs, changes to permitted uses for certain Services, and the introduction of safety requirements for when our Services are used for real-time navigation or in applications intended for real-time driving. We are removing clauses with the same meaning or effect as the [above listed provisions](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/faq#tos-updates) from the [EEA-specific Google Maps Platform Service Specific Terms](https://cloud.google.com/terms/maps-platform/eea/maps-service-terms). The Google Maps Platform Services listed below will have new service-specific terms or technical changes. You can refer to the service specific integration guides linked below for additional information. | Services with Technical Changes | Services with New Terms Restrictions | |---|---| | *These APIs behave differently in the EEA region* **Maps** - [Maps Static API](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/maps-static) - [Map Tiles API](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/map-tiles) **Environment** - [Solar API](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/solar) **Mobility** *Technical changes will propagate to your project within 1-3 days after you accept the EEA Terms*. | **Maps** - [Street View Static API](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/street-view-static) **Routes** - [Directions API (Legacy)](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/directions) - [Distance Matrix API (Legacy)](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/distance-matrix) - [Roads API](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/roads) - [Routes API](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/routes) - [Routes Preferred API](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/routes-preferred) **Places** - [Address Validation API](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/address-validation) - [Geocoding API](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/geocoding) - [iOS Geocoder within Maps iOS SDK](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/ios-geocoder) - [Places API (New and Legacy)](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/places) **Mobility** | At this time, only the Services listed above are changing. You will be able to continue using them as is, for unmodified integrations, without the [three ToS provisions](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/faq#tos-updates). ### Why is Google Maps Platform making these Services and terms changes? #### Standards for Google Maps Content Due to our standards for Google Maps Content, we are making adjustments to some of the Google Maps Platform Services for **new** integrations within your Customer Applications. For example, if the EEA ToS applies to your integration, and you want to display the Places-related content with a map, you should now use the Places UI Kit to display the content instead of Places API (New and Legacy). #### Road safety EEA customers may now use Google Maps Platform Services, where suitable, in embedded vehicle systems. They may also use Google Maps Platform Services, where suitable, for real-time navigation with a third-party map, as long as that real-time navigation usage complies with Google's safety requirements. Due to road safety risks that can arise under these new terms, Google now requires that developers adhere to [safety requirements](https://cloud.google.com/terms/maps-platform/eea-safety-requirements), in order to, for example, limit the risks of mismatched roads. Please note: use of the Google Maps Platform Services in embedded vehicle systems in the EEA occurs at each customer's own discretion and the customer is responsible for compliance with any applicable laws, regulations, industry standards, or other requirements. ### Are any new Services being introduced at this time? We will continue to launch new services. At this time, we are bringing to General Availability the Places UI Kit (Javascript, Android, iOS) to provide map-related visualization use cases for continued support for our developers. This Service can be used with any map, including third-party maps. Refer to the [Places API (New and Legacy) service-specific integration guide](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/places#uikit) for more information. ## Your current integration of Google Maps Platform prior to 8 July 2025 ### How will these changes impact my current integration of Google Maps Platform Services? To help you with these changes, you may continue using Google Maps Platform in your Customer Application(s) for your current project's Google Maps Platform integrations, with the three ToS provisions waived. Your existing integration is considered in an "unmodified state" as long as it is not materially modified on or after **8 July 2025**. After **8 July 2025**, projects which are created with a billing account in the EEA or moved from a non-EEA billing account to an EEA billing account are not eligible for the unmodified state. You are free to modify your integration and transition your integration out of the unmodified state at any time. If you do so on or after **8 July 2025** , an individual with the full legal authority must accept the [EEA ToS](https://cloud.google.com/terms/maps-platform/eea) in the Console for the project, to continue using our Services. Project Owners and Project Editors have the permissions necessary to accept the EEA ToS. You can update the permissions for individuals on your account in the Console. If you have a negotiated agreement with Google, refer to the question, [How do these updates impact me if I have a negotiated agreement with Google?](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/faq#negotiated-agreement) ### How do I accept the EEA ToS? As a Project Owner or Project Editor, you can accept the EEA ToS in the following ways: - Accept the EEA ToS on the [Google Maps Platform Support page](https://console.cloud.google.com/google/maps-apis/support) of the Console. - When you perform actions in the Console that will require you to accept the EEA ToS, such as enabling a new Generally Available Google Maps Platform Service or migrating project ownership from a non-EEA billing account to an EEA billing account, the Console will prompt you to accept the EEA ToS. ### Which Terms of Service govern my integration during the unmodified state? As long as your [integration](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/faq#integration) remains in the unmodified state, these [Google Maps Platform Terms of Service](https://cloud.google.com/maps-platform/terms) will continue to apply, with Google waiving the following 3 provisions: - No Re-Creating Google Products or Features - No Use With Non-Google Maps - No Use in Embedded Vehicle Systems Google will also waive clauses with the same meaning or effect as the above listed clauses in all other applicable contractual terms that govern your use of Google Maps Platform, including the Google Maps Platform Service Specific Terms. If you have a negotiated agreement with Google, that agreement will govern your use of Google Maps Platform Services while your integration is in the unmodified state, with Google waiving the three clauses mentioned above and clauses with the same meaning or effect. ### What does an integration in a Customer Application mean? Integration means the use of Google Maps Platform Services within a Customer Application, via a **dedicated project**, to fulfill a distinct end-user purpose or workflow. Each distinct purpose or workflow so fulfilled is a separate integration. For example, if a Customer Application has a store locator that allows users to search for a store near them, and in a separate workflow offers an online store checkout; the store locator integration and the online checkout integration are considered separate integrations within the Customer Application. Google will treat all integrations associated with a project as being in the same state. As a best practice, we recommend that developers use one project per integration. ### How do I transition my integration out of the unmodified state? If you make a material modification to your integration, your integration will transition out of the unmodified state, and you'll need to accept the EEA ToS, as described in [How will these changes impact my current integration of Google Maps Platform Services?](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/faq#affect-current-integration) A material modification occurs when an EEA Customer: (i) uses new functionality of a new or existing General Availability Google Maps Platform Service within an existing integration, or (ii) makes changes to how third party services are used with Google Maps Platform Services within the integration. Google may make updates to this definition and the examples from time to time, and changes to the definition will apply only going forward to subsequent changes that are made. Please refer to the bottom of this page for the change log. #### Examples of material modifications *If you*: - Maintain an existing integration, but update to newer versions of the Services in order to access new functionality. - Maintain the same integration, but enable an additional General Availability Service in the integration. - Maintain the same integration, but query new methods in the Service, or start using new response fields from the Service. - Maintain the same integration, but expand to other platforms (for example, Android). - Have an integration with no map, and start using a Google or third-party map, or replace an existing map. If the addition of functionality to your integration (for example, new platform, new features) is implemented with a new project, that new project will be governed by the EEA ToS and the existing project remains in the "unmodified state." #### Examples that are not material modifications (can stay in "unmodified state") *If you maintain the same integration and*: - Update to a newer version of the Services for security, compatibility, accessibility, or other issue/bug resolution reasons; as long as no new functionality is used. - Make administrative or security updates (for example, setting API quotas, restricting an API key, replacing a restricted API key, or configuring budget alerts). - Change your billing model. - Change visual details of the user interface (for example, color and font). - Move a project to a new billing account. - Expand geographic coverage of the integration without using new functionality. ## Other questions ### Are pricing changes part of these updates? No, pricing is not changing as part of this update. ### Will there be EEA-specific SKUs? No, SKUs will remain the same. ### How do these updates impact me if I have a negotiated agreement with Google? If you have a negotiated agreement with Google, and you materially modify your project's Google Maps Platform integration in your Customer Application, you must adhere to the EEA-specific Google Maps Platform Service Specific Terms, which, starting **8 July 2025**, will be incorporated into your negotiated agreement with Google. ### Why did I receive a notice? You received a notice because you are a project owner, billing administrator, or essential contact associated with a project(s) linked to a billing account with an EEA address. Refer to [Who is affected by these changes?](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/faq#who-is-affected) question for more information on who is affected by these changes. ### I received multiple notices, which one is applicable? You may have received multiple notices if you are associated with multiple billing accounts, where at least one of these accounts has a negotiated agreement with Google. Refer to the notice you received for additional information. If you have additional questions you may [contact us](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/faq#additional-questions). ### How do these updates impact me if I am a Maps Partner? For more information about how these changes might affect you, contact your Partner Development Manager. ### What do I need to do to prepare for these changes? We encourage you to familiarize yourself with all the content in this document and the [service-specific integration guides](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/faq#sst-updates) to ensure new integrations and material modifications to existing integrations comply with the Services and term changes. - Review the list of APIs you are using on your project (with [Usage Reports](https://developers.google.com/maps/reporting-and-monitoring/reporting#usage-rpt) or billing account with [Billing Reports](https://developers.google.com/maps/reporting-and-monitoring/reporting#billing-rpt))). - For each of the APIs you are using, check if there are [technical or contractual changes](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/faq#sst-updates). ### What if I have additional questions not covered in this FAQ? If you have any technical questions not addressed in this or the [service-specific integration guides](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/faq#sst-updates), you can contact [Google Maps Platform Support](https://developers.google.com/maps/support?utm_medium=DevSite&utm_content=GMP_Support). If you have a negotiated agreement with Google and have questions about your contract, you can contact your Google Maps Platform representative. If you are unsure who your account representative is, please reach out using our [Contact Sales form](https://mapsplatform.google.com/contact-us/?utm_medium=DevSite&utm_content=Contact_Sales).

The terms review found a blocker: Place IDs may be retained, but I found no published permission to retain Places names/addresses for the workshop’s lifetime and export them to Calendar. EEA terms also require a permitted-use assessment.

I’m recording the field-by-field rules and proposed lookup contract while keeping ALE-442 gated. Manual destinations can proceed independently.

Success. Updated the following files:
M docs/google-places-terms-validation.md
M docs/google-maps-venue-design.md

*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: /Users/alessandrojcm/repos/dhc-dashboard/docs/google-places-terms-validation.md
@@
 provisioning, billing/key changes, live acceptance, activation or backfill.
 
+## Decision and gate status
+
+**Google-derived saved destinations and Calendar export remain gated.** Public
+terms support retaining Place IDs and fetching fresh details for permitted
+in-app use. They do not establish permission for the agreed durable
+name/address-to-Calendar workflow. The relevant billing account and agreement
+have not been inspected. This is an engineering compliance decision on public
+evidence, not legal advice or a determination of the club's actual contract.
+
+The manual path remains supported independently: a required staff-owned short
+label, optional independently supplied destination name/address and optional
+validated manual Maps link. Those facts may be saved in each source domain and
+projected into native Calendar `location` through the existing protocol.
+Do not copy a Places result into the manual path and rename its provenance.
+No manually entered destination needs a provider identity or a Places lookup.
+
+[ALE-442](https://linear.app/alessandrojcm/issue/ALE-442/venues-shared-google-autocomplete-across-workshop-forms)
+must not ship its Google path on the strength of this report. Keep the agreed
+native Calendar location goal; neither a description-link workaround, an
+ID-only destination nor manual retyping of provider text silently replaces it.
+
+## Applicable terms: verified rules and missing account facts
+
+| Public evidence | Consequence for this integration |
+| --- | --- |
+| Both general and EEA Maps terms select EEA applicability by **billing account address**, with an exception for a pre-8-July-2025 project integration remaining unmodified. Ireland is in the FAQ's EEA list. | Club geography, server region and attendee location do not establish the account's terms. New Places functionality cannot inherit an exception merely because Calendar OAuth already exists. [General terms][terms], [EEA terms][eea-terms], [FAQ][eea-faq]. |
+| The FAQ describes additional services, methods and response fields as material modifications, and treats integrations in a project as having the same state. It warns that it is a point-in-time reference. | Read the current agreement first. Do not enable Places in an existing project or accept new terms to test this assumption. [FAQ][eea-faq]. |
+| General terms §3.2.3(a)-(b) and EEA terms §3.3.2(a)-(b) prohibit export outside the Services, copying/saving business names and addresses, and caching unless expressly permitted. | Saving a selected venue is still storage. Refreshing every 30 days does not legalize fields without a caching exception. [General terms][terms], [EEA terms][eea-terms]. |
+| Both Service Specific Terms A.3 allow Google-ID caching. Places B.14.3 (general) / B.15.4 (EEA) permit latitude/longitude caching for up to 30 consecutive days. The Places policy explicitly allows indefinite Place-ID storage. | The identifier exception does not extend to names, addresses, URLs or an entire result. Coordinates are outside this feature and its lookup mask. [General SST][sst], [EEA SST][eea-sst], [Places policy][policies]. |
+| EEA SST B.15.1 prohibits non-ID/non-coordinate Places content "With any Map"; its definition includes linking, except a link to the content's source map. B.15.2 limits that content to enumerated permitted uses. | A no-map suggestions UI can support address autocomplete under permitted use (1). That does not establish ongoing venue display, generated directions links or Calendar exports. Uses (2), (4), (6) and (8) have specific store, productivity, financial-transaction or social-platform contexts; none is assumed to cover this club workflow. [EEA SST][eea-sst], [permitted uses][eea-uses]. |
+| The EEA integration guide permits provider-supplied source links and ID/coordinate-only map linking. Places UI Kit is exempt from the two EEA restrictions above. | An arbitrary generated link containing Places text is not automatically the source-link exception. UI Kit changes display integration, not the default storage/export rules, so it does not solve durable Calendar locations. No switch to UI Kit is approved here. [EEA guide][eea-guide], [EEA SST][eea-sst]. |
+| The street-address Autocomplete exception applies only when the end user could otherwise have supplied the address completely/accurately, solely for that user's specific transaction. It excludes suggestion lists, other content and POI/address lookups from other services. | The selected venue name and Details address are not made unrestricted by a staff click. This proposed POI-plus-Details workflow does not rely on the narrow street-address exception. [Places policy][policies]. |
+
+The general and EEA terms pages inspected say last modified **26 August 2026**;
+both SST pages say **28 October 2026**; the EEA permitted-uses page says
+**4 June 2025**. These public versions are evidence, not confirmation of the
+club's accepted, negotiated or reseller terms.
+
+### Owner evidence needed to close the gate
+
+Record the following without putting keys, billing details or private contracts
+in this public repository:
+
+1. The intended project, linked billing account's EEA/non-EEA classification,
+   agreement/version and any negotiated/reseller terms that affect this use.
+   If claiming the unmodified-integration exception, supply its project/workflow
+   history and why introducing these Places calls does not end it. The safe
+   planning assumption for a new EEA integration is current EEA terms.
+2. A contract/legal assessment or written licensing provision that permits the
+   exact fields to be retained for workshop history and exported to Calendar,
+   including guest copies, update messages and the historical no-rewrite policy.
+   Identify the duration and deletion/refresh requirements. A recurring API call
+   cannot delete an address already sent to guests.
+3. If EEA terms apply, the exact permitted-use category covering each staff and
+   attendee use beyond address lookup, and the map/source-link treatment of
+   attendee directions and Calendar's native navigation. If no category fits,
+   obtain a suitable license or bring the blocker back for a scope decision.
+4. An attribution treatment that remains compliant in native Calendar clients,
+   plus required application terms/privacy notices. The existing source
+   projection and Calendar `location` string do not carry a structured Place or
+   attribution contract. [Calendar Events][calendar], [Services list][services].
+
+Google technical support cannot grant terms exceptions; the policy directs
+contract interpretation to counsel and custom licensing to Sales. This task
+has not contacted either, accepted terms or accessed the Console.
+[Places policy][policies]. Once documentary permission is established, update
+this record and the affected ticket before implementing Google-derived storage.
+Native Calendar UX acceptance remains a separately authorized ALE-445 task.
+
+## Field-by-field destination contract
+
+"Transient" below means only the current permitted lookup/display interaction,
+with no reusable cache or durable copy. There is **no approved numeric cache
+TTL** for Places text here. All Google display permissions remain conditional
+on the applicable terms and attribution; this table does not enable the feature.
+
+| Field / origin | Display and permitted use | Persistence, refresh and deletion | Calendar export |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Existing short label, independently staff-authored | Existing workshop/email copy; keep it separate from provider text and the Beginners' Workshop 80-character limit unchanged. | Existing domain lifetime; no Places refresh. Never overwrite automatically from `displayName`. | Existing label fallback is unaffected. |
+| Manual destination name/address and optional manual Maps link, independently supplied | Staff and attendee destination display; link validation still applies. | Source-owned storage; replace/clear explicitly, preserve on omission. Manual replacement removes stale Google identity/derived links. | Native name/address permitted by this Places assessment; UX remains to be checked. Do not put the link in the event description. |
+| Autocomplete `text.text` / structured prediction text | Suggestions only, with Google Maps attribution. Do not treat the prediction as resolved Details fields. | Transient; discard on replacement/abandonment/unmount. No database, logs, snapshots, persistent form drafts or fixtures of real responses. | No. |
+| Details `displayName.text` | Selected-result preview and fresh permitted in-app display, with attribution. Attendee display needs its own permitted-use assessment. | No durable storage permission established. Fetch fresh for a permitted interaction; discard afterwards. Neither a 30-day cache nor lifetime retention is approved. | Gated: no published exception established. |
+| Details `formattedAddress` | Same as name. This Details address does not inherit the narrow Autocomplete street-address exception. | Same as name. Do not store the address in a constructed URL or short label to evade the rule. | Gated: no published exception established. |
+| Place ID (`id`, autocomplete `placeId`) | Lookup identity; may be used in Maps URLs subject to the applicable linking rules. It is not a human-readable destination. | Indefinite ID storage permitted. Keep an application timestamp and refresh IDs older than 12 months as Google recommends, using Details `id` only. Remove on explicit destination clear/replacement. A failed/obsolete/moved ID requires review, never automatic selection or relocation. | No ID-only substitute: Calendar has no ordinary structured Place-ID location field. |

# Skill: writing-for-agents

Reference for writing any document an agent consumes — a skill, an `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`, a doc reached by a pointer. The packaging differs; the writing does not: the same levers make each one predictable — the agent taking the same _process_ every run, not producing the same output.

When the document you're writing is a skill, read [`SKILL-MECHANICS.md`](SKILL-MECHANICS.md) for frontmatter, invocation choice, and router skills.

## Context pointers

A **context pointer** is a reference held in the agent's context that names some out-of-context material and encodes the condition for reaching it. A skill's description is one; a line in `AGENTS.md` naming a doc is the same object. The pointer's _wording_, not its target, decides when the agent reaches the material — and how reliably. A must-have target behind a weakly worded pointer is a variance bug: sharpen the wording first, and inline the material only if sharpening fails.

A pointer does two jobs — state what the material is, and list the **branches** that should trigger reaching it (a branch is a distinct case the document handles, so different runs take different paths through it). Every word of an always-loaded pointer costs on every turn, so it earns even harder pruning than the body:

- **Front-load the leading word** — the pointer is where it does its triggering work.
- **One trigger per branch.** Synonyms that rename a single branch are one branch written twice; collapse them and keep only genuinely distinct branches.
- **Cut identity the body already carries.**

## The two loads

Every document and pointer you add spends one of two budgets:

- **Context load** — the cost of always-loaded material on the agent's window: an `AGENTS.md` line, a skill description, anything sitting in context every turn, spending tokens and attention whether or not it fires.
- **Cognitive load** — the cost on the human: which documents exist and when to reach for each. The human is the index. Not a cost to minimise — it is the price of human agency; spend it where human judgement matters, remove it where it does not.

Material reached only through a pointer escapes context load at the price of the pointer's own line; material with no pointer at all rides entirely on cognitive load.

## Information hierarchy

A document is built from two content types — **steps** (the ordered actions the agent performs) and **reference** (definitions, rules, facts consulted on demand) — that mix freely: all steps (a recipe), all reference (a review's rules, this skill), or both. The core decision is where each piece sits on the **information hierarchy**, a ladder ranked by how immediately the agent needs the material:

1. **In-file step** — the primary tier: what the agent does, in order.
2. **In-file reference** — consulted on demand. Often a legitimately flat peer-set (every rule of a review on one rung) — a fine arrangement, not a smell.
3. **Disclosed reference** — pushed out into a separate file, reached by a context pointer, loaded only when the pointer fires. Spans a sibling file in the same folder through fully external reference that lives anywhere and any document can point at.

Push too little down and the top bloats; push too much and you hide material the agent actually needs. That tension is the whole decision.

**Progressive disclosure** is the move down the ladder — out of the main file and behind a pointer — so the top stays legible. Not primarily a token optimisation: it is how the hierarchy is protected. Branching is the cleanest disclosure test: inline what every branch needs, and push behind a pointer what only some branches reach. When a document has steps, in-file reference that should be disclosed buries them and turns attending to them into a coin-flip — a variance lever, not just a legibility one.

**Co-location** is the within-file companion: where the ladder decides _how far down_ a piece sits, co-location decides _what sits beside it_ once there. Keep a concept's definition, rules, and caveats under one heading rather than scattered, so reading one part brings its neighbours with it. The test: the document should read like documentation written for the agent — grouped material reads that way; scattered material does not. (Distinct from duplication: that repeats one meaning in two places; scattering fragments one meaning across many.)

**Sprawl** is the failure mode here: a document simply too long, even when every line is live and unique. Attention thins across the excess, and every extra line is one more to keep relevant. The cure is the ladder: disclose reference behind pointers, and split by branch or sequence so each path carries only what it needs.

## Steps and completion criteria

Every step ends on a **completion criterion** — the condition that tells the agent the work is done. Two properties make it a lever:

- **Clarity** — can the agent tell done from not-done? A vague bound ("understanding reached") invites **premature completion**: ending the step before it is genuinely done, attention slipping to _being done_. The visible steps still ahead — the **post-completion steps** — supply the pull; the criterion's clarity is the resistance. Defend in order: **sharpen the bound first** (local and cheap); only if it is irreducibly fuzzy _and_ you observe the rush, hide the later steps by splitting the sequence — and hiding only works across a real context boundary (a hand-off or a subagent dispatch; an inline call leaves the later steps in context and clears nothing).
- **Demand** — how much it requires. "Every modified model accounted for" forces thorough work where "produce a change list" does not. Demand drives **legwork** — the digging the agent does within the work, latent in the wording rather than written as its own step — and it is not step-bound: "every rule applied" binds a body of flat reference just as "every step done" binds a sequence, which is how an all-reference document still carries an exhaustiveness bar.

The strongest criteria are both checkable and exhaustive.

## When to split

Splitting one document into two spends one of the two loads, so split only when the cut earns it:

- **By sequence** — split a run of steps where the post-completion steps tempt the agent to rush the one in front of it. Keeping them out of view drives more legwork on the current task. Beware the reverse: merging sequences exposes each step's later steps to what follows, inviting premature completion.
- **By invocation** — skill-specific: see [`SKILL-MECHANICS.md`](SKILL-MECHANICS.md).

## Leading words

A **leading word** is a compact concept already living in the model's pretraining that the agent thinks with while running the document (_lesson_, _fog of war_, _tracer bullets_). Repeated as a token, never as a sentence, it accumulates a distributed definition and anchors a whole region of behaviour in the fewest tokens, by recruiting priors the model already holds. Coining your own works if you define it clearly, but a made-up word recruits no priors — you pay in definition tokens what a pretrained word gives free; reach for an existing word first.

It anchors twice. In the body, _execution_: the agent reaches for the same behaviour every time the word appears, and inside flat reference it focuses attention on a class of thing to look for. In a pointer, _invocation_: when the same word lives in your prompts, your docs, and your codebase, the agent links that shared language to the material and reaches it more reliably.

Hunt for opportunities to refactor with leading words. A triad spelled out at three sites, a pointer spending a sentence to gesture at one idea — each is a passage begging to collapse into a single token:

- "fast, deterministic, low-overhead" → _tight_ (a _tight_ loop).
- "a loop you believe in" → _red_ — a fuzzy gate becomes a binary observable state (the loop goes _red_ on the bug, or it doesn't).

You win twice: fewer tokens, and a sharper hook for the agent to hang its thinking on. Assume every document is carrying restatements that leading words retire — go find them.

**Negation** is the failure mode beside this lever: steering by prohibition drags the forbidden behaviour into context and makes it _more_ available, not less. _Don't think of an elephant_, and the elephant is all there is; the negation is a weak modifier the strongly-activated concept overruns, so the ban half-reads as an instruction to do the thing. Prompt the **positive** — state the target behaviour ("write one-line comments") so the banned one is never spoken. A prohibition earns its place only as a hard guardrail you cannot phrase positively; even then, pair it with the positive target so attention lands on what to do.

## Pruning

- Keep each meaning in a **single source of truth**: one authoritative place, so changing the behaviour is a one-place edit. **Duplication** — the same meaning in more than one place — costs maintenance and tokens, and inflates a meaning's prominence on the ladder past its real rank. (The accidental inverse of a leading word, which repeats a token on purpose, never the meaning.)
- The **environment** is a source of truth too — `package.json` scripts, config files, the directory layout, `--help` output — and a document that restates it is a **cache**: a copy of a lookup, earning its load only when the lookup is expensive. Cache what the agent cannot find by looking: the unwritten convention, the reason behind a choice, the gotcha no config confesses. Leave the one-file, one-command lookups to the environment, where they cannot go stale.
- Check every line for **relevance**: does it still bear on what the document does? A line loses relevance by never bearing on the task (mere exposition, or a branch that should be disclosed) or by going stale as the behaviour or world it describes changes. Shorter documents are easier to keep relevant. Without a pruning discipline the default fate is **sediment**: stale layers that settle because adding feels safe and removing feels risky, until you must core down through them to find what is still live.
- Hunt **no-ops** sentence by sentence: an instruction the model already obeys by default pays load to say nothing. The test — does it change behaviour versus the default? — is model-relative, not reader-relative: two people disagreeing about a no-op disagree about the default, and settle it by running the document, not by debate. When a sentence fails, delete the whole sentence rather than trim words from it. The test also grades leading words: a word too weak to beat the default (_be thorough_ when the agent is already thorough-ish) is a no-op, and the fix is a stronger word (_relentless_), not a different technique.

- Check every line for **relevance**: does it still bear on what the document does? A line loses relevance by never bearing on the task (mere exposition, or a branch that should be disclosed) or by going stale as the behaviour or world it describes changes. Shorter documents are easier to keep relevant. Without a pruning discipline the default fate is **sediment**: stale layers that settle because adding feels safe and removing feels risky, until you must core down through them to find what is still live.
- Hunt **no-ops** sentence by sentence: an instruction the model already obeys by default pays load to say nothing. The test — does it change behaviour versus the default? — is model-relative, not reader-relative: two people disagreeing about a no-op disagree about the default, and settle it by running the document, not by debate. When a sentence fails, delete the whole sentence rather than trim words from it. The test also grades leading words: a word too weak to beat the default (_be thorough_ when the agent is already thorough-ish) is a no-op, and the fix is a stronger word (_relentless_), not a different technique.

  ┊ 100 │ +The Place-ID refresh recommendation and indefinite-ID permission come from the

  ┊ 102 │ +indicates a moved place must not move a published workshop. Refreshing display

  ┊ 106 │ +
  ┊ 107 │ +## Attribution and user notices
  ┊ 108 │ +
  ┊ 109 │ +For any later permitted Google path, implement and test these obligations from
  ┊ 110 │ +the [current Places policy][policies], general terms §3.2.2 and EEA terms
  ┊ 111 │ +§§3.2.2/3.2.4 plus SST A.2:
  ┊ 112 │ +
  ┊ 113 │ +- Suggestions need visible **Google Maps** attribution in the same visual
  ┊ 114 │ +  container as the Google list. Use Google's official logo where possible;
  ┊ 115 │ +  "Google Maps" text is allowed where space is limited. Do not use an old
  ┊ 116 │ +  "powered by Google" example as the specification for a new implementation.
  ┊ 117 │ +- The resolved selection needs attribution beside its Google name/address,
  ┊ 118 │ +  even after the suggestions close. Render returned data-provider names/links
  ┊ 119 │ +  too. Escape and validate these fields; do not inject provider HTML.
  ┊ 120 │ +- Any permitted attendee display needs the same associated branding/provider
  ┊ 121 │ +  credits on every member, external-attendee and safe Intake surface, not just
  ┊ 122 │ +  a footer on the staff form. A directions link alone is not attribution.
  ┊ 123 │ +- Preserve result/credit association on retained licensed content, including
  ┊ 124 │ +  read models and any export where the permission requires it. A Place ID or
  ┊ 125 │ +  `provider: google` marker alone is not visible attribution. Calendar is a
  ┊ 126 │ +  separate unresolved export surface; being another Google product does not
  ┊ 127 │ +  prove compliance.
  ┊ 128 │ +- Visually distinguish provider facts from the staff-owned label/manual data;
  ┊ 129 │ +  do not suggest Google supplied manual values. Follow Google's current logo
  ┊ 130 │ +  sizing, clear-space, legibility and accessible-name requirements. Text
  ┊ 131 │ +  attribution must remain "Google Maps", unmodified, untranslated and unwrapped,
  ┊ 132 │ +  with the documented accessible typography. Do not hide credits on mobile.
  ┊ 133 │ +- Application terms must notify users of Google Maps features/content and link
  ┊ 134 │ +  the Google Maps End User Additional Terms and Google Privacy Policy as the
  ┊ 135 │ +  applicable agreement requires. Review the app's privacy/consent notices
  ┊ 136 │ +  before activation; these requirements are not satisfied by this repository
  ┊ 137 │ +  document. [General terms][terms], [EEA terms][eea-terms].
  ┊ 138 │ +
  ┊ 139 │ +## Lookup integration
  ┊ 140 │ +
  ┊ 141 │ +The technical choice is **Places API (New) REST: Autocomplete (New), then Place
  ┊ 142 │ +Details (New) on deliberate selection**, called by Phoenix through one
  ┊ 143 │ +domain-neutral Req/Req.Test boundary. It has no Workshop IDs, source writes or
  ┊ 144 │ +Calendar authority. A supported HTTP integration does not by itself authorize
  ┊ 145 │ +retention or Calendar export; the terms decision below governs those uses.
  ┊ 146 │ +[Autocomplete guide][autocomplete], [Details guide][details].
  ┊ 147 │ +
  ┊ 148 │ +Choose a custom suggestions UI rather than a Google JavaScript widget so the
  ┊ 149 │ +existing shared form and UI primitives can own keyboard interaction and manual
  ┊ 150 │ +fallback. No Maps JavaScript loader, map, browser Google key, staff geolocation,
  ┊ 151 │ +Geocoding API, Routes API or venue directory is required by this choice.
  ┊ 152 │ +
  ┊ 153 │ +### Application-facing lookup contract
  ┊ 154 │ +
  ┊ 155 │ +These are proposed boundary shapes, not implemented endpoints or a database
  ┊ 156 │ +schema. Later HTTP exposure is OpenAPI-first and capability-gated for the staff
  ┊ 157 │ +who can use the relevant forms; the lookup is not a public arbitrary Google
  ┊ 158 │ +proxy. Both source domains keep their own save commands.
  ┊ 159 │ +
  ┊ 160 │ +| Operation | Input | Closed output |
  ┊ 161 │ +| --- | --- | --- |
  ┊ 162 │ +| Suggest | Venue query and a fresh opaque search-session token | `ready` with ordered `{placeId, text}` suggestions (including an empty list), or `unavailable` with a closed reason |
  ┊ 163 │ +| Resolve | The explicitly selected `placeId` and that session token | `ready` with `{provider: "google", placeId, name, address, attributions}`, or `unavailable` with a closed reason |
  ┊ 164 │ +
  ┊ 165 │ +`name` and `address` in a resolved result are transient Google-derived preview
  ┊ 166 │ +text, not proof that either field may be saved. `attributions` is a closed list
  ┊ 167 │ +of `{provider, uri}` obtained from Google's attribution fields; Google Maps
  ┊ 168 │ +branding is an additional display obligation. Do not return raw Google JSON,
  ┊ 169 │ +credentials, error bodies, arbitrary URLs, photos, reviews or coordinates.
  ┊ 170 │ +
  ┊ 171 │ +Suggested failure vocabulary is `not_configured | disabled | invalid_input |
  ┊ 172 │ +not_found | quota | provider_unavailable`. Authentication/configuration errors
  ┊ 173 │ +are monitored without exposing their upstream response. No result is an ordinary
  ┊ 174 │ +empty success. Bound input size, rate and request duration, and check the
  ┊ 175 │ +caller's capability before spending provider quota. A session token is a billing
  ┊ 176 │ +correlator, never authorization or a source-workflow credential.
  ┊ 177 │ +
  ┊ 178 │ +### Provider request and response mapping
  ┊ 179 │ +
  ┊ 180 │ +1. Suggest uses `POST https://places.googleapis.com/v1/places:autocomplete`,
  ┊ 181 │ +   `Content-Type: application/json` and server-only `X-Goog-Api-Key`.
  ┊ 182 │ +   The JSON body contains `input`, `sessionToken`, `languageCode: "en"`,
  ┊ 183 │ +   `regionCode: "ie"` and this fixed application bias:
  ┊ 184 │ +
  ┊ 185 │ +   ```json
  ┊ 186 │ +   {
  ┊ 187 │ +     "locationBias": {
  ┊ 188 │ +       "circle": {
  ┊ 189 │ +         "center": { "latitude": 53.3498, "longitude": -6.2603 },
  ┊ 190 │ +         "radius": 30000
  ┊ 191 │ +       }
  ┊ 192 │ +     }
  ┊ 193 │ +   }
  ┊ 194 │ +   ```
  ┊ 195 │ +
  ┊ 196 │ +   The Dublin centre/radius are application choices, not a venue coordinate
  ┊ 197 │ +   requirement. Omit `locationRestriction`, `includedRegionCodes`, type filters
  ┊ 198 │ +   and `origin`. Leave query predictions and pure service-area businesses off.
  ┊ 199 │ +   `locationBias` permits results outside the circle; `regionCode` influences
  ┊ 200 │ +   ranking/formatting without a country exclusion. Do not rely on the server's
  ┊ 201 │ +   IP-derived default bias. [Request reference][autocomplete-reference].
  ┊ 202 │ +
  ┊ 203 │ +2. Set `X-Goog-FieldMask` to
  ┊ 204 │ +   `suggestions.placePrediction.placeId,suggestions.placePrediction.text.text`.
  ┊ 205 │ +   Map only `suggestions[].placePrediction.placeId` and `.text.text` into the
  ┊ 206 │ +   closed suggestion. Render that text as text, not HTML. Do not parse it into a
  ┊ 207 │ +   destination name/address: prediction text can differ from Details. Ignore
  ┊ 208 │ +   unsupported prediction variants; an empty or omitted suggestions array is
  ┊ 209 │ +   empty success. [Autocomplete fields][autocomplete-reference].
  ┊ 210 │ +
  ┊ 211 │ +3. Resolve uses `GET https://places.googleapis.com/v1/places/{placeId}` with the
  ┊ 212 │ +   Place ID encoded as one path segment, fixed host/path construction,
  ┊ 213 │ +   `sessionToken` and `languageCode=en` query parameters, and server-only
  ┊ 214 │ +   `X-Goog-Api-Key`. Do not set a Details `regionCode`, so an Irish country name
  ┊ 215 │ +   is not deliberately omitted from the full address. Use exactly
  ┊ 216 │ +   `X-Goog-FieldMask: id,displayName,formattedAddress,attributions`.
  ┊ 217 │ +   Map `id`, `displayName.text`, `formattedAddress` and
  ┊ 218 │ +   `attributions[].{provider,providerUri}`. In New, `name` is the resource name
  ┊ 219 │ +   `places/…`, not the human-readable `displayName`. Missing required identity
  ┊ 220 │ +   or useful destination text cannot be repaired by guessing from a suggestion;
  ┊ 221 │ +   offer manual entry. [Details guide][details], [Place reference][place].
  ┊ 222 │ +
  ┊ 223 │ +4. Generate a random UUID v4 per interaction. Use the same token for all its

  ┊ 226 │ +   new token for replacement. Never reuse an Intake, login, acceptance or

  ┊ 239 │ +### Data leaving the application
  ┊ 240 │ +
  ┊ 241 │ +Places receives the venue query or selected Place ID, random session token,
  ┊ 242 │ +fixed language/region/bias, field mask and authentication. Google also observes
  ┊ 243 │ +the server's network metadata. Construct fresh outbound requests; do not forward
  ┊ 244 │ +browser cookies, authorization, client-IP headers, Referer or a page URL.
  ┊ 245 │ +Search controls must warn staff to enter venue information only. Do not attach

  ┊ 257 │ +
  ┊ 258 │ +Use the documented universal URL format when a permitted destination is

  ┊ 264 │ +

  ┊ 266 │ +`destination_place_id=<encoded Place ID>` can also be supplied; `destination`
  ┊ 267 │ +is still required. Google-derived destination text remains gated. Build with a URL encoder,
  ┊ 268 │ +omit `origin`, and respect the 2,048-character URL limit. Maps URLs need no API
  ┊ 269 │ +key. This is a link, not a fetched/cached route. It does not add structured Place
  ┊ 270 │ +identity to Calendar's free-form location field. [Maps URLs][maps-urls].
  ┊ 271 │ +
  ┊ 272 │ +Do not request or persist `googleMapsUri`: its documented meaning is a URL for

  ┊ 279 │ +
  ┊ 280 │ +## Configuration and operational readiness

  ┊ 306 │ +  sessions revert to per-request charges. The owner must review current rates,

--- COMMIT SYNTAX ---
Create a commit.

By default, all uncommitted changes of the checkout but runs in are included in the commit: the main
worktree's, or a linked worktree's when run from inside one. This can be controlled with change
flags such as --empty and --interactive, or by providing CHANGES as positional arguments.

Run from a linked worktree, or given changes from one, the commit is placed at the tip of that
worktree's branch. Otherwise, if there are no branches applied, a new branch is created for the
commit. If there is only one stack of branches applied, the commit is placed at the tip of that
stack. Otherwise, the targeting flags --above, --below and --branch control where the commit is
placed. --above and --below are mutually exclusive; combine either with --branch to name a new
branch when targeting a branch.

The commit is expected to have a commit message unless --no-message is provided. If none of

Because [Google’s published terms](https://cloud.google.com/maps-platform/terms) explicitly restrict **copying and saving business names and addresses** returned by Places.

Our plan was to save those results and put them into Calendar.

There **is** an exception for street-address autocomplete where someone selects an address they already know. But that doesn’t clearly cover searching for a venue/business and saving its Place Details.

I hadn’t established whether your Google agreement permits our exact use.

**So I found a licensing uncertainty—not proof that we can’t do it.** I should have presented that distinction clearly instead of making it sound like a definitive prohibition.

1: # Workshop destinations: Google Places validation (ALE-439)
2: 
3: Validated against public Google documentation on 6 November 2026 for
4: [ALE-439](https://linear.app/alessandrojcm/issue/ALE-439/venues-validate-places-terms-and-permitted-destination-data).
5: The [confirmed venue design](google-maps-venue-design.md) and
6: [ALE-438](https://linear.app/alessandrojcm/issue/ALE-438/spec-workshop-venue-autocomplete-and-directions)
7: remain the product scope. This document authorizes no implementation, Google
8: provisioning, billing/key changes, live acceptance, activation or backfill.
9: 
10: ## Decision and gate status
11: 
12: **Google-derived saved destinations and Calendar export remain gated.** Public
13: terms support retaining Place IDs and fetching fresh details for permitted
14: in-app use. They do not establish permission for the agreed durable
15: name/address-to-Calendar workflow. The relevant billing account and agreement
16: have not been inspected. This is an engineering compliance decision on public
17: evidence, not legal advice or a determination of the club's actual contract.
18: 
19: The manual path remains supported independently: a required staff-owned short
20: label, optional independently supplied destination name/address and optional
21: validated manual Maps link. Those facts may be saved in each source domain and
22: projected into native Calendar `location` through the existing protocol.
23: Do not copy a Places result into the manual path and rename its provenance.
24: No manually entered destination needs a provider identity or a Places lookup.
25: 
26: [ALE-442](https://linear.app/alessandrojcm/issue/ALE-442/venues-shared-google-autocomplete-across-workshop-forms)
27: must not ship its Google path on the strength of this report. Keep the agreed
28: native Calendar location goal; neither a description-link workaround, an
29: ID-only destination nor manual retyping of provider text silently replaces it.
30: 
31: ## Applicable terms: verified rules and missing account facts
32: 
33: | Public evidence                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Consequence for this integration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
34: | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
35: | Both general and EEA Maps terms select EEA applicability by **billing account address**, with an exception for a pre-8-July-2025 project integration remaining unmodified. Ireland is in the FAQ's EEA list.                                                                    | Club geography, server region and attendee location do not establish the account's terms. New Places functionality cannot inherit an exception merely because Calendar OAuth already exists. [General terms][terms], [EEA terms][eea-terms], [FAQ][eea-faq].                                                                                                                                   |
36: | The FAQ describes additional services, methods and response fields as material modifications, and treats integrations in a project as having the same state. It warns that it is a point-in-time reference.                                                                     | Read the current agreement first. Do not enable Places in an existing project or accept new terms to test this assumption. [FAQ][eea-faq].                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
37: | General terms §3.2.3(a)-(b) and EEA terms §3.3.2(a)-(b) prohibit export outside the Services, copying/saving business names and addresses, and caching unless expressly permitted.                                                                                              | Saving a selected venue is still storage. Refreshing every 30 days does not legalize fields without a caching exception. [General terms][terms], [EEA terms][eea-terms].                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
38: | Both Service Specific Terms A.3 allow Google-ID caching. Places B.14.3 (general) / B.15.4 (EEA) permit latitude/longitude caching for up to 30 consecutive days. The Places policy explicitly allows indefinite Place-ID storage.                                               | The identifier exception does not extend to names, addresses, URLs or an entire result. Coordinates are outside this feature and its lookup mask. [General SST][sst], [EEA SST][eea-sst], [Places policy][policies].                                                                                                                                                                           |
39: | EEA SST B.15.1 prohibits non-ID/non-coordinate Places content "With any Map"; its definition includes linking, except a link to the content's source map. B.15.2 limits that content to enumerated permitted uses.                                                              | A no-map suggestions UI can support address autocomplete under permitted use (1). That does not establish ongoing venue display, generated directions links or Calendar exports. Uses (2), (4), (6) and (8) have specific store, productivity, financial-transaction or social-platform contexts; none is assumed to cover this club workflow. [EEA SST][eea-sst], [permitted uses][eea-uses]. |
40: | The EEA integration guide permits provider-supplied source links and ID/coordinate-only map linking. Places UI Kit is exempt from the two EEA restrictions above.                                                                                                               | An arbitrary generated link containing Places text is not automatically the source-link exception.
